AfterRoomEntered.rationale: Gorget.cs:21-28 applies PowerVar<PlatingPower>(4m).BaseValue to its owner on AfterRoomEntered when the room `is CombatRoom`; the sim uses on_combat_start, the combat-scoped hook, with the same amount and the same applier (the owner). This is EXACTLY the mechanism audit/records/relic/bronze_scales.json already verdicted deliberate-divergence for BronzeScales.cs's identical AfterRoomEntered(CombatRoom) + PowerCmd.Apply body -- one verdict per mechanism, binding rule 3, matched and not re-derived. Sequence checked rather than assumed: CombatRoom.cs:225-229 fires Hook.AfterRoomEntered AFTER CombatManager.SetUpCombat but BEFORE AfterCombatRoomLoaded starts the combat, so in C# the Plating lands slightly earlier than Hook.BeforeCombatStart (turn_structure spec step 3) while the sim applies it during it. Same observable: Plating is a per-combat power on both sides, no ported BeforeCombatStart listener reads the player's powers, and the player enters every fight -- and only a fight -- with 4 Plating. EXECUTED (py audit/tools/relic_probes_b07.py gorget-plating): combat start gives powers={'plating': 4} and block 0; the turn-1-end slot gives block 4; turn 2 opens with block cleared and Plating at 3. Rule 7: bronze_scales.json, CombatRoom.cs and the turn_structure record are not hashed by this record.

guards.what: N1: the `room is CombatRoom` type test (Gorget.cs:23) is what makes the divergent hook choice safe
guards.rationale: C# fires AfterRoomEntered for EVERY room and self-filters to combat rooms, so binding the port to on_combat_start reproduces the filter for free. Same reasoning and same verdict as bronze_scales guard N1 (binding rule 3). A port that used the sim's run-level after_room_entered (relics/base.py:194) without a room-type check would try to apply a power outside combat, where the sim has no container to hold it. Rule 7: relics/base.py and bronze_scales.json are not hashed by this record.

guards.what: N2: `base.DynamicVars["PlatingPower"].BaseValue` (Gorget.cs:26) -- the key is the POWER TYPE NAME, not 'Plating'
guards.rationale: PowerVar<PlatingPower>(4m) (line 19) registers under the generic argument's type name, which is why the read is the keyed form. Value 4, no AscensionHelper branch in the file, and the sim's literal 4 (gorget.py:17) matches. Same idiom bronze_scales guard N2 records for ThornsPower; picking the wrong var name silently yields 0.

guards.what: N3: `PowerCmd.Apply<PlatingPower>(ctx, Owner.Creature, amount, Owner.Creature, null)` passes applier = the OWNER (Gorget.cs:26); the sim passes applier=self.player (gorget.py:17)
guards.rationale: PowerCmd.cs:67's signature is (choiceContext, target, amount, applier, cardSource), so the fourth argument is the applier and it is the player's own creature -- matched exactly. This matters because relic/unsettling_lamp's doubling and several power guards branch on the applier: contrast relic/belt_buckle guard N3, where BOTH sides pass null. Here both sides pass the player, so the two relics are correctly distinguished. cardSource is null on both sides, so no card-sourced interaction exists. Rule 7: PowerCmd.cs and belt_buckle.json are not hashed by this record.

guards.what: N4 (DORMANT): PlatingPower's own port diverges on WHERE it decays -- the sim decays from on_player_turn_start (pre-draw) where PlatingPower.cs:70-83 decays from AfterSideTurnStart (post-draw)
guards.issue: MECHANISM: PlatingPower.cs:70-83 decrements in AfterSideTurnStart with a `TurnNumber != 1` guard for a player owner (turn_structure spec step 23, after the hand draw); powers.py:1063-1074's PlatingPower._decay runs from on_player_turn_start with `combat.turn > 1`, which the executed hook order (py audit/tools/relic_probes.py turn-order) places BEFORE modify_hand_draw and the draw. So for a window of one draw the sim's Plating amount is one lower than the game's. RECORDED AT GORGET'S SITE BECAUSE GORGET IS THE ONLY PORTED PLAYER-SIDE SOURCE OF PLATING (`grep -rn PlatingPower sts2_rl/ --include=*.py` outside powers.py returns relics/gorget.py and the enemy-side appliers), but the DIVERGENCE BELONGS TO THE POWER, not the relic -- audit/records/power/ does not exist yet, so no record owns it and none is issued here beyond this flag. DORMANT: nothing in the draw window reads a Plating amount (no ported modify_hand_draw listener or draw-time effect consults it), and the block Plating grants is computed at turn END from the then-current amount, which is the same number on both sides. Goes live with any turn-start effect between the two slots that scales off a Plating stack. VERIFIED SAFE FOR THE COMBAT-START GRANT, which is the half that could have broken Gorget outright: PlatingPower.cs:41-55's BeforeSideTurnStart returns early `if (base.Owner.IsPlayer)`, so the game does NOT give a Plating-holding player block at combat start, and powers.py:1054-1056 gates the same grant on `self.owner.side == 'enemy'` -- executed (probe gorget-plating): block 0 at combat start on both sides. Rule 7: sts2_rl/powers.py, PlatingPower.cs and relics/base.py are not hashed by this record.
